title: improv·artist · computational (Vera Molnar)
mutation_directive: improv artist: computational via Vera Molnar

improv_extras.practice: algorithmic line drawings 1960s onward; deviation from the grid as expression

v1.feedback: Strong marriage of Lucy silhouette with Molnar's quantised-angle vocabulary — the four systematic angles plus breathing deviation is a genuine reading of her practice, not decoration. The cream-on-sepia palette reads like aged plotter paper, which is exactly right. Two refinements: increase uHalfLen slightly (0.18–0.22) so individual strokes read as deliberate marks rather than stipple at distance, and tighten the depth-fade falloff so the back of the figure doesn't dissolve into invisibility — Molnar's drawings hold density edge-to-edge.

v2.feedback: Strong Molnar translation — quantized angles with breathing deviation is genuine to her practice, and the cream-on-ink palette is restrained and warm. The main weakness is that strokes ignore surface normals: all 42k segments rotate in the XY plane regardless of the Lucy surface they sit on, which flattens the 3D read into a somewhat poster-like silhouette rather than a sculptural volume. A refined version should sample the face normal at each point and project the Molnar angle into the tangent plane, so strokes on the cheek foreshorten differently from strokes on the shoulder, giving the form real curvature depth. The depth-fade sepia gradient partially compensates but normal-aligned strokes would make this exceptional.
